title: 16-Layer Alternating Stack with Stochastic Jitter Initialization
scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 12 to 16 while applying ±20% stochastic initialization jitter will disrupt symmetric phase-coupling bottlenecks observed in prior 12L runs, enabling access to adjacent resonance orders and improving the dual-band spectral separation between 300-450 nm reflection and 1000-1700 nm transmission.
design_principle: Alternating HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave-inspired stack with randomized thickness initialization to escape local minima; gradient-based thickness optimization within expanded bounds (±35% of median quarter-wave thickness at 1350 nm reference).
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (16 finite layers total, 8 HfO2 + 8 SiO2 pairs)
design_variables: thickness optimization bounds (±35% of median quarter-wave thickness)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and SiO2 compatible with plasma ion-assisted deposition
layer thicknesses should remain above 40 nm for process control
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for plane-wave propagation through isotropic layered media
Thin-film interference principles for dual-band spectral control
Stochastic initialization to escape local minima in non-convex optimization landscapes
expected_advantages: 16 layers provides more degrees of freedom than 12L prior runs while remaining computationally tractable
Jitter initialization breaks symmetry that may have trapped 12L optimization
Expanded bounds allow exploration of adjacent resonance orders
known_risks: May converge to similar local minimum as 12L if landscape is rugged
Increased layer count may reduce robustness to thickness variations
HfO2 absorption in UV may limit 300-450 nm reflectance
execution_request_english: Optimize a 16-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence using HfO2 and SiO2. Stack sequence: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica. Initialize all 16 layer thicknesses with uniform random jitter of ±20% around quarter-wave optical thickness at 1350 nm reference wavelength (HfO2 ~155 nm physical, SiO2 ~230 nm physical based on typical indices). Apply gradient-based thickness optimization with bounds of ±35% from initial median thickness. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Compute mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band and mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band. Total layer count fixed at 16 finite layers. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: reflection in 1000-1700 nm; transmission in 300-450 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30.
revision_reason: Increased layer count from 12 to 16 to explore intermediate complexity between prior 12L and excluded 20L configurations; applied feedback directive for ±20% stochastic jitter initialization and ±35% expanded thickness bounds to escape local minima.
